analyst_view.overall: Second-placed Roma (30 points, four straight wins, 5-1 at Parma with four goals from Malen) host Monza, 14th with 10 points, who ended a run of four defeats by beating Fiorentina on 23 November. Roma play PSG in Paris in the Champions League on Wednesday night with their European campaign at risk, so some rotation on Sunday is possible; Pellegrini and Rensch are out and Balerdi is doubtful, while Dybala and Svilar are back. Monza's Ivan Juric, Roma's coach for a short spell in 2024, has said Maye, Folorunsho and Ngonge are out, and the numbers do not know about these absences; former Roma defender Ziolkowski is fit again. The numbers already lift Roma a lot for their recent shooting and scoring, and no referee is named yet.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.7 goals, already boosted by Roma's 22 goals in their last six (including 5-1 at Parma). Monza lose two attacking players, Folorunsho and Ngonge, that the numbers still count on, and Roma may rotate a few players four days after a hard Champions League night in Paris. I lean lower by 5%, about 3.5.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.3 corners, already lifting Roma for their 43 corners in six games and trimming Monza for their low count. Juric's Monza play a 3-4-2-1 with wing-backs and tend to defend deep away from home, which feeds Roma's corners, but the numbers already see that pattern. I stay at about 9.3.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.9 cards, with Roma's quiet recent record (8 cards in six) already counted. No referee has been named; Juric returning to the Olimpico adds a little edge, but nothing the numbers cannot see in Monza's usual card count. I stay at about 3.9.

shots.text: The numbers say 29.3 shots, already raising Roma by 16% for their 112 shots in six games. Monza's attack loses Ngonge and Folorunsho, who the numbers count, and Roma's fitness after Paris is a question, so I lean slightly lower, about 28.4.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 11.2 shots on target, already lifted strongly for both sides' recent accuracy (Roma +18%, Monza +11%). Monza without Folorunsho and Ngonge should test the Roma keeper less, and Roma's recent burst of finishing is unlikely to stay that high every week, so I lean lower, about 10.8.
